full_judgment:
2. Their case, in short, is that their mother Parbati Bala Gharami took pattan of the suit land comprising an area of 3.90 acres, from the original recorded owners. She along with her another co-sharer instituted Title Suit No. 402 of 1958 against those landlords and others and got a compromise decree on 23-1-59 in respect of her share is said 3.90 acres of land and since pattan she had been possessing the same, which are now being possessed by the plaintiffs. On 8-9-93 the Vested Property Authority at the instance of some interested persons of the locality illegally issued notice upon the plaintiffs claiming 1.53 acre out of the suit land as Vested Property and accordingly they started the aforesaid VP Case, although there is no legal basis for the same. 

 4. The trial Court dismissed the suit holding, inter alia, that the plaintiffs could not prove the basis of taking pattan of the suit land by their mother, Parbati Bala Gharami and that the defendant also could not prove the legal foundation of enlisting in the alleged census report the property as vested property (Ext. Ka).The trial Court, however, found the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land. The lower appellate Court set aside the decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit holding, inter alia, that the plaintiff-respondents, on the basis of Ext. 1 (Ka) and 1 (Kha) namely, the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 402 of 1958 and the compromise petition dated 23-8-59 respectively proved, their title to the suit land and that by Ext. 2 series, 21 dakhilas, the certified copy of the khatians, opened in their mother's name on the basis of the decree of the aforesaid title suit and Ext. 3 series Choukidari Tax receipts and the oral evidence proved their possession and title in the suit land and that the defendant could not prove the foundation of making the suit property as vested property. The High Court Division refused to interfere with these findings of fact in revision.
